body: I think we should reserve some time for introspection again. Would be good to know what things people would like to see improved, who is interested in helping improve things, and what keeps people from improving things.

I would like to discuss [Fetch Retry](https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1838). Will there be a joint session with WebPerfWG too? I've been told if there's a joint WHATWG-WebPerf WG session, it would be best to discuss it at that time, so that I can get feedback for the overall API shape and also iron out the details on the behavior etc.
I would like to put the [menu elements proposal](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11729) on the WHATWG agenda for discussion as well.

I'd like to request stage 2 on https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11542 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/2142, and https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11669 https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11669. Also discuss if anything is missing in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11542 outside of those. 

PRs: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11818 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11631

Depending on where we will be with Navigation API spec issues in a couple of weeks, there might be a topic to discuss - how to ensure better match between implementations and the spec. This applies especially to Navigation API, but is a more generic topic. Implementations should follow the spec and not do explicitly something else - if something else is needed (because of webcompat or failing WPTs or such) one should file a spec issue.

Some recent Navigation API spec issues
https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues?q=label%3A%22topic%3A%20navigation%22%20type%3ABug

I guess this is a bit related to annevk's [comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11711#issuecomment-3389296206).

I'd like to discuss HTML-in-Canvas, hoping to advance this to stage 2:
- https://github.com/WICG/html-in-canvas
- https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10650
- https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11588

I'm also interested in the declarative out-of-order streaming and APIs for streaming HTML mentioned by @noamr above.

We'd like to revive https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/127 - and perhaps discuss more generally a pattern where one-shot events have equivalent promises, as we often see buggy websites with timing issues because they miss a DOMContentLoaded event, or a image `load` event for example.

https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/127
https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/1936
https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4594#issuecomment-489337027
https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7419

Elements which fetch subresources might be interesting to discuss: `iframe`, `script`, `link`, `style`, `picture`, `audio`, `video`, `img`. Some of these are not so much "one-shot" as they will be replaced if the `src` changes, however they are timing sensitive so there is good motivation for these to be included.

It would be good to decide what to do with ShadowRealms. There are tests testing APIs in ShadowRealms and some specs (at least WebIDL)  mentions them, but _if_ ShadowRealms won't happen, things should be cleaned up.
Proposing to add https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11743 as well to discuss what is the best way to model such an optimization and how to standardize it.

I'd like to talk a bit about [<meta name="rating" ...>](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11722) to provide some context and gauge implementer interest. More context will also be provided in [the age-based restriction breakout session](https://github.com/w3c/tpac2025-breakouts/issues/75) on Monday
I'd like to discuss the best way to make progress on focus-without-user-activation, #11839.
On the tooling side, I'd like to give an update on [migrate from Wattsi to Bikeshed](https://github.com/whatwg/html-build/issues/297) for the HTML spec.

We'd like to discuss couple blocking issues on Scoped Custom Element Registry. Ideally in a time block friendly to Pacific Standard Time, as some speakers will be attending remotely.

- https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11858
- https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1413
I'd like to discuss https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11847
I would be happy to also discuss https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11819.

base appearance for list box select elements: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11477
definition of list box and drop down box select elements: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8189

I'd like to discuss the AsyncContext web integration (#10432), possibly moving it to stage 1, as well as the related topic of how the TC39 and WHATWG stages process should work together for web integrations of TC39 proposals.

This shouldn't conflict with the AsyncContext discussion on WebPerf WG, which is on Tuesday 14:00-15:00. Other than that, it would be better for me if it was scheduled on Tuesday rather than Thursday, but that's not a hard requirement.
I would like to discuss https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10673. Ideally in a time block friendly to Pacific Standard Time, as I'll be attending remotely.

I'd love to discuss #11641, I'll be remote, so ideally, we can have a time block friendly to Pacific Standard Time.

Specifically, I'd like to go over the [explainer on Open UI ](https://open-ui.org/components/scoped-focusgroup.explainer/) and my latest [spec draft](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11723)

I'd like to discuss https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11599 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11600. I think we're close to being able to land these, so let's do a final check-in and see if anything else is needed. (I am sort of inheriting this from Domenic now that he is retired, so I'm a little less up to speed on it than others).
I'd also like to discuss https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8013. I'm trying to pull some concrete concrete proposal out of it to see if we can resolve it.

I'd like to discuss FormControlRange:

- https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11478
- https://github.com/whatwg/dom/pull/14044- 
- #11741
If possible, I'd like to discuss https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1839. It's about providing an opt-in for no-cors requests to be considered readable (for things like static public resources).
